newsitem.title: USA: Detailed breakdown of Vermont jobless markets.
newsitem.headline: Detailed breakdown of Vermont jobless markets.

text.p: Vermont's Department of Employment and Training has released a detailed breakdown of February unemployment rates in the state's key labor markets.
--Barre-Montpelier, 5.8 pct in Feb, down from 6.4 pct in Jan and 6.9 pct a year ago.
--Bennington-Manchester, 5.0 pct, down from 5.2 pct in Jan and 5.4 pct a year ago.
--Burlington, 3.3 pct, down from 3.4 pct in Jan and 3.8 pct a year ago.
--Enosburg, 10.1 pct, down from 11 pct in Jan and 11.2 pct in Feb.
--Hartford-Lebanon, Vermont, New Hampshire, 2.4 pct, up from 2.2 pct in Jan but down from 3.0 pct a year ago.
--Keene-Brattleboro, Vermont only, 3.3 pct, down from 3.5 pct in Jan and 4.1 pct a year ago.
--Middlebury, 5.7 pct, down from 5.9 pct in Jan and 6.8 pct a year ago.
--Morristown-Stowe, 6.2 pct, down from 6.4 pct in Jan and 7.5 pct a year ago.
--Newport, 10.2 pct, down from 11.2 pct in Jan and 11.6 pct a year ago.
--Randolph, 4.6 pct down from 4.7 pct in Jan and 5.3 pct a year ago.
--Rutland, 5.0 pct, unchanged from Jan, but down from 5.4 pct a year ago.
--St Johnsbury, 6.7 pct, down from 7.2 pct in Jan and 7.1 pct a year ago.
--Springfield, 4.4 pct, unchanged from Jan but down from 5.4 pct a year ago.
